text.p: The National Science Foundation Tuesday said it would give the late Carl Sagan, a noted astronomer and Pulitzer Prize-winning author, the agency's Distinguished Public Service Award for lifetime achievement.
The award is the NSF's highest honour given to a private citizen for contributions to the agency's activities in science and education.
"Carl Sagan didn't just popularise science, he explained its relevance in ways the general public could understand and appreciate," said NSF Director Neal Lane.
Sagan, who spent his life investigating the possibility of life in outer space, died Dec. 20 after a two-year struggle with bone marrow cancer.
NSF said it would present the award to Sagan's widow, Ann Druyan, at a dinner on May 7.
